decision: Keep the repository war-room as the controlling source until the fields stabilize; mirror approved fields into WordPress admin later.
implementation_spec: The repo continues to hold CSV, HTML, screenshots, audits, and source manifests. WordPress receives only stable registry fields after owner review.
why_this_way: This prevents a rushed admin build from becoming another disconnected store of partial research.
acceptance_gate: Every admin field must trace back to a repo file, row id, screenshot, or approved source note.

decision: Create a private WordPress admin content type named ndl_keyword_registry for keyword and page ownership.
implementation_spec: Register it on init, show it in admin, keep it out of public search and public URLs, enable revisions and REST only for controlled admin integration.
why_this_way: A private registry gives writers one controlled place to check ownership without exposing strategy publicly.
acceptance_gate: Admin users can create, filter, revise, export, and review registry rows without public archive pages.

decision: Store canonical keyword owner, URL owner, page template, funnel role, language, status, writer gate, source gate, legal gate, asset gate, last review date, and internal-link targets.
implementation_spec: Use registered meta or ACF field groups. Every field needs sanitization, permissions, and import/export mapping.
why_this_way: The anti-cannibalization system only works if writers cannot publish from memory or guesswork.
acceptance_gate: A registry row cannot be marked approved unless owner, URL, status, and gate fields are complete.

decision: Build list views for money pages, city hubs, project pages, professional pages, foreign-investor pages, guides, missing pages, stale pages, and blocked pages.
implementation_spec: Use native list table columns or Admin Columns Pro for filter, sort, inline edit, bulk edit, and export.
why_this_way: The owner needs a live worktable, not a hidden document archive.
acceptance_gate: A non-technical manager can filter all open Tel Aviv buyer keywords, all stale pages, and all blocked writer items in under one minute.

decision: Use custom workflow statuses for idea, assigned, writing, source check, legal check, asset check, owner review, ready to build, published, refresh needed, and blocked.
implementation_spec: Use custom statuses and planner views for editorial governance; do not rely only on post drafts.
why_this_way: A draft/published binary state is too weak for money keyword governance.
acceptance_gate: A content item visibly shows which gate is blocking it and who owns the next action.

decision: Block or warn before publishing if content lacks keyword owner, canonical URL owner, source notes, legal gate, asset truth, and internal links.
implementation_spec: Implement as an admin pre-publish validation layer for posts, pages, projects, listings, and guides.
why_this_way: This is the practical protection against SEO cannibalization and thin content.
acceptance_gate: A writer cannot publish a money page that conflicts with an existing canonical owner or lacks required gates.

decision: Use an editorial planner for scheduled pages, refresh cycles, assignments, and backlog status.
implementation_spec: PublishPress Planner can provide calendar and overview. Keep strategic registry ownership separate from task scheduling.
why_this_way: Calendar tools are useful for delivery timing, but they are not the source of keyword truth.
acceptance_gate: The calendar shows when pages are planned or refreshed, while the registry still owns keyword decisions.

decision: Use a project-management plugin only for execution tasks, not for canonical keyword ownership.
implementation_spec: WP Project Manager can track Kanban, milestones, task reporting, and responsibility, but it must link back to registry ids.
why_this_way: Generic task boards do not prevent content cannibalization by themselves.
acceptance_gate: Every task card includes registry id, page id, owner, screenshot gate, and acceptance notes.

decision: Add an admin evidence panel that links to desktop and mobile screenshots, visual QA notes, source documents, and release checks.
implementation_spec: Each major page or registry row should reference saved screenshots and QA notes in the repo.
why_this_way: The owner asked for screenshot proof, not verbal completion claims.
acceptance_gate: A row without required screenshots is visibly incomplete and cannot be marked ready.

decision: Require asset status fields for real, reused, illustrative, missing, or contractor needed.
implementation_spec: Attach source, license/permission, capture date, and replacement plan.
why_this_way: Real estate pages lose trust when placeholder images are treated as real.
acceptance_gate: Any project page or listing detail shows internal asset truth before public publication.

decision: Store paid-placement and commercial-ordering status internally, then expose only clean public disclosure copy where needed.
implementation_spec: Use Hebrew public labels for commercial disclosure. Do not expose internal ranking terms or build labels to users.
why_this_way: The site must be commercially honest without leaking internal terminology.
acceptance_gate: Public pages show clean disclosure where required; admin rows show the commercial state and evidence.

decision: Create a controlled event dictionary before implementation: page view, project open, unit select, map interaction, phone tap, WhatsApp tap, form start, form submit, consultant request, interior request, investor-language switch, contractor-intake submit.
implementation_spec: Each event gets name, trigger, page type, required parameters, privacy notes, destination, and QA method.
why_this_way: The funnel cannot be monetized without measurable buyer and contractor intent.
acceptance_gate: Every revenue action appears in the dictionary and has a screenshot or debug proof after implementation.

decision: Build a private KPI dashboard after events are stable: traffic, leads, project engagement, unit interest, language interest, source quality, contractor pipeline, and revenue status.
implementation_spec: Start with GA/GTM/CRM exports or REST-driven admin cards. Do not invent numbers.
why_this_way: The owner needs a business cockpit, but fake metrics are worse than no metrics.
acceptance_gate: Dashboard cards show real source and last updated date for every metric.

decision: Separate owner, strategist, writer, editor, developer, contractor, and viewer roles.
implementation_spec: Use capabilities so only trusted users can approve registry ownership, legal gates, paid states, and publication clearance.
why_this_way: The registry becomes dangerous if every writer can change money-page ownership.
acceptance_gate: Only approved roles can change canonical owner, status approved, and public release gates.

decision: Support CSV import/export for keyword registry, page owners, screenshots, and release state.
implementation_spec: Round-trip exports must preserve row ids and not silently overwrite newer admin edits.
why_this_way: The user moves between machines and agents; the system must remain portable.
acceptance_gate: A fresh site can import the registry package and recreate the same ownership map.

decision: Create a repeatable bootstrap package for future WordPress real-estate sites after NadLan stabilizes.
implementation_spec: Package folders, templates, registry CSV, owner HTML template, screenshot gates, and admin field schema.
why_this_way: The same method must work later without relying on external design credits.
acceptance_gate: A new site can be initialized with the same war-room folders, registry schema, and screenshot contract.
